title: Knowledge Systems: The New GTM Stack — Jeffrey Wang, Exa
talk_summary: Exa's co-founder describes treating go-to-market as a data/engineering problem: an ICP dashboard built on semantic web search, a customer-signal alerting system, a dozen Slack-accessible agents over internal data, and a 'Jeffbot' clone of himself calibrated with evals from his past decisions. He closes with principles: API-first access for agents, crystallized GUIs alongside chat, and arbitrarily customizable SaaS (e.g. Salesforce MCP) over build-vs-buy.

takeaways.technique: Caller-scoped permissions on a privileged agent
takeaways.what_they_do: The same agent identity has full read/write across company systems when the founder calls it, but when anyone else calls it, it can only draft messages and is denied most MCP tools.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when anybody else calls Jeffbot all can do is draft messages and also I don't give Jeffbot permissions to all of our MCPs

takeaways.technique: Evals distilled from historical human decisions
takeaways.what_they_do: He mined hundreds of past decisions from Slack and email, wrote them up as a decision framework, and turned them into evals used to calibrate the clone agent's behavior.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I analyzed them and I created evals. So, I actually created evals from those decisions and calibrated this agent system

takeaways.technique: API-first internal data access for agents
takeaways.what_they_do: Every internal and external system is exposed through a programmatic interface (MCP/CLI) so agents can read and act on it; without good APIs agents have no data access.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if there did not exist really good APIs on top of any internal and external data we'd be we'd be out of luck

takeaways.technique: Shared agent fleet over internal data in chat
takeaways.what_they_do: About a dozen agents live in Slack, all with access to internal data, and any team member can query any of them for account research or demos.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have like maybe a dozen different agents inside of our Slack and anybody can use any of them

takeaways.what_they_do: A 'Request Lens' system fires alerts whenever something significant happens (signup, heavy usage, churn, VIP), giving the team a concrete queue to act on.
takeaways.evidence_quote: anytime something significant happens with any of our customers, we're alerted

takeaways.technique: Crystallized UI plus flexible chat, not chat-only
takeaways.what_they_do: He argues against making everything a chatbot: keep stable, learnable UIs for recurring use cases and reserve free-form chat agents for arbitrary queries.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there is something really nice about being able to visit the same consistent UX for the same use cases over time
